problem: Free users who wanted privacy had to pay or move to competitors.
title: GitHub makes private repositories free for small teams
context: GitHub previously charged for private repositories, while public repositories were free.
decision_made: Give free accounts unlimited private repositories, limited to three collaborators per repository.
action_taken: Announced in January 2019 together with a simplified Enterprise offering; the paid developer plan was renamed GitHub Pro.
observed_outcome: Not documented in the sources used.
lessons: Capping collaborators rather than repositories keeps the free tier useful for individuals while leaving teams a reason to pay.
limitations: No adoption or revenue results were found. GitHub's owner, Microsoft, may have had different incentives from an independent company.

claims.claim_text: GitHub Free accounts got unlimited private repositories with up to three collaborators each.
The announcement was paired with a unified Enterprise offering.
